title_tag: 美国中期选举前夕：亚裔和拉美裔，为什么正在成为最有价值的选民？—— 英国《经济学人》外刊讲解第1214天
h1: 美国中期选举前夕：亚裔和拉美裔，为什么正在成为最有价值的选民？
category: 英国《经济学人》外刊讲解 第1214天

headline.en_html: The Americans changing politics for the better — Hispanics and Asians have become their country’s most dynamic swing voters
headline.zh: 这些正在让美国政治变好的美国人——拉丁裔和亚裔，已经成了美国最有活力、也最摇摆的选民

notes.en: the Americans (n.) means a particular, identified group of American people rather than Americans in general
notes.ctx: the + 复数，特指某一群特定的美国人，而非泛指全体。标题先抛出一个模糊的大概念“美国人”，吊着读者往下看副标题揭晓“到底是谁”——这是制造悬念的标题写法。
notes.ex1: The Americans are becoming more diverse than ever. （这群）美国人正变得比以往更加多元。
notes.ex2: The Americans who built this country came from every corner of the world. 建立这个国家的美国人来自世界各地。

notes.en: for the better means in a way that improves a situation, making it better than before
notes.ctx: 灵魂在 for：表达方向、趋势。changing 是中性的，加 for the better 锁死方向——是往好了改。反义 for the worse（变坏）。
notes.ex1: The situation took a turn for the worse. 情况急转直下、变糟了。
notes.ex2: It’s a change for the better. 这是往好了变，是件好事。

notes.en: Hispanics (n.) means people of Spanish or Latin American origin living in the US
notes.ctx: 词根 Hispania 是古罗马对伊比利亚半岛的称呼。与 Latino（强调“来自拉丁美洲”的地理概念）区分：巴西人讲葡萄牙语，是 Latino 而不算 Hispanic；西班牙本土移民算 Hispanic 不算 Latino。
notes.ex1: Hispanics are the fastest-growing segment of the US electorate. 拉美裔是美国选民中增长最快的群体。
notes.ex2: Many Hispanics trace their roots to Mexico and the Caribbean. 许多拉美裔的根可以追溯到墨西哥和加勒比地区。

notes.en: dynamic (adj.) means constantly changing, full of energy and new ideas
notes.zh: 有活力的，灵活多变的，能搅动局面的
notes.ctx: 不是干巴巴的“动态的”，而是“身上有股劲儿、有股能搅动局面的力量”，与标题 changing 呼应：他们是在使劲改变，不是站那儿等。
notes.ex1: She is one of the most dynamic figures in the industry. 她是这个行业里最有活力的人物之一。
notes.ex2: The region has one of the most dynamic economies in the world. 该地区拥有全球最具活力的经济体之一。

notes.en: swing voters (n.) means people who are not loyal to one political party and may vote for different parties in different elections
notes.ctx: 全文最核心概念。swing 本义“荡”，如秋千：这次荡到蓝营、下次荡到红营。与“铁票”（base voter）相对——真正决定胜负的是这群能荡来荡去的人。
notes.ex1: Candidates spend most of their money chasing swing voters. 候选人把大部分钱都花在争取摇摆选民上。
notes.ex2: Swing voters often decide the outcome of close elections. 摇摆选民往往决定势均力敌选举的结果。

paragraphs.en_html: Midterm elections are always a <mark class="voc">referendum</mark> on the <mark class="voc">sitting</mark> American president, but rarely has an <mark class="voc">incumbent</mark> so <mark class="voc">wilfully</mark> put himself in the <mark class="voc">spotlight</mark> <mark class="voc">in defiance of</mark> his own unpopularity. As the campaign ends, Donald Trump is <mark class="voc">commandeering</mark> rallies in Republican <mark class="voc">strongholds</mark>, a sign of his party’s <mark class="voc">vulnerability</mark> and his <mark class="voc">unwavering</mark> faith in his own <mark class="voc">star power</mark>. Away from the spotlight, however, something more surprising—and more important—has been happening: Hispanics and Asians have emerged as America’s most valuable voters.
paragraphs.zh: 中期选举，向来是对现任总统的一场全民打分。可几乎没有哪一位在任者，会像他这般，明知道自己不受待见，还偏要迎着聚光灯往上站。随着选战收官，川总正在共和党的大本营里，强占一场又一场的集会——这既暴露了他所在政党的虚弱，也印证了他对自己明星光环的顽固迷信。然而，聚光灯照不到的地方，一件更令人意外、也更重要的变化，正在悄然发生：拉丁裔和亚裔，已经悄然崛起，成为美国当下最值钱的选民。

notes.en: referendum (n.) means a vote in which all the people in a country or area are asked to give their opinion about an important question
notes.ctx: 词根拉丁语 referre“带回去、提交回去”，即把一件事交回给人民决定。此处是比喻：中期选举名义上选议员，实际是老百姓对总统满意与否的打分——美国宪法里并没有全国性公投，这个“其实不存在的公投”更添讽刺。
notes.ex1: The government decided to hold a referendum on the issue. 政府决定就这一问题举行全民公投。
notes.ex2: The country voted in a referendum on independence. 这个国家在全民公投中就独立问题进行了投票。

notes.en: sitting (adj.) means currently holding a particular office
notes.ctx: sitting president 直译“正坐在（白宫）那把椅子上的人”，比 current president 更有画面感。同类：sitting member（现任议员）。
notes.ex1: The sitting governor is seeking re-election. 这位现任州长正在寻求连任。
notes.ex2: No sitting president has lost a primary challenge in modern times. 现代以来，还没有哪位在任总统在初选挑战中落败。

notes.en: incumbent (n.) means the person who currently holds a particular official position
notes.ctx: 词根拉丁语 incumbere：in- 在……上 + cumbere 躺、靠，“正占着这把椅子、坐在上面的人”。前脚 sitting、后脚 incumbent，一个意思两个说法，用词讲究。
notes.ex1: The incumbent is seeking a second term. 这位现任者正在谋求连任。
notes.ex2: Incumbents usually have a big advantage in elections. 现任者通常在选举中拥有很大优势。

notes.en: wilfully (adv.) means deliberately, doing something on purpose, often something wrong
notes.zh: 任性而故意地，明知故犯地
notes.ctx: 不是“不小心”，是“明知故犯、偏偏要”——明知道自己不受欢迎，偏要往聚光灯下钻。
notes.ex1: He wilfully ignored the warnings. 他故意无视了那些警告。
notes.ex2: He wilfully broke the rules to make a point. 他故意违反规则来表达立场。

notes.en: spotlight (n.) means a strong light used to light up a particular person or area on a stage
notes.zh: 聚光灯；万众瞩目的中心
notes.ctx: 全段首尾呼应的关键词：川总把自己塞进 spotlight，真正重要的却发生在 away from the spotlight。镜头由明到暗、由闹到静，是全文的点睛之笔。
notes.ex1: His little brother always steals the spotlight. 他弟弟老抢他风头。
notes.ex2: She has been in the spotlight since winning the election. 自从赢得选举以来，她一直处在聚光灯下。

notes.en: in defiance of means openly refusing to obey, against
notes.ctx: defiance：de- 分开、对抗 + fid 信任（同 faith），“不再信任、公然反抗”。in defiance of his own unpopularity＝明知道自己不受欢迎，却偏要跟这个事实对着干。
notes.ex1: She stayed in the job in defiance of her doctor’s advice. 她无视医生的建议，继续留在那个岗位上。
notes.ex2: He continued the speech in defiance of the protesters. 他不顾抗议者，继续演讲。

notes.en: commandeer (v.) means to officially take possession or control of something, especially for military purposes, or to seize something for your own use
notes.ctx: 1881 年才进英语，来自南非荷兰语 kommanderen“下命令、征调”：当年英军直接把当地人的马、车、房子征用。作者用它说川总强占共和党大本营的集会——attend 是出席、hold 是举办、commandeer 是强占，动词选得毒。
notes.ex1: Soldiers commandeered vehicles to cross the river. 士兵们强征车辆渡河。
notes.ex2: The rebels commandeered the radio station. 叛乱分子强占了广播电台。

notes.en: stronghold (n.) means an area where support for a particular party is very strong
notes.zh: 堡垒，要塞；（政党的）大本营、铁票区
notes.ctx: strong 强 + hold 守住的地方。Republican strongholds＝共和党的铁票区。
notes.ex1: The south has long been a stronghold of the ruling party. 南方长期以来一直是执政党的铁票区。
notes.ex2: The city is a Democratic stronghold. 这座城市是民主党的堡垒。

notes.en: vulnerability (n.) means the state of being easy to hurt or attack
notes.ctx: 词根 vulner 来自拉丁语 vulnus“伤口”。川总跑回自己大本营拉票，说明这个党心里没底了，是“脆弱”的信号。
notes.ex1: The scandal exposed the candidate’s vulnerability. 这桩丑闻暴露了这位候选人的软肋。
notes.ex2: Small states worry about their economic vulnerability. 小国担心自身经济的脆弱性。

notes.en: unwavering (adj.) means not changing or becoming weaker
notes.ctx: un- 不 + waver 摇晃、动摇（与 swing 同家族）。unwavering faith in his own star power＝对自己明星光环“铁了心”的深信不疑。
notes.ex1: She has shown unwavering support for the team. 她对这支队伍给予了坚定不移的支持。
notes.ex2: He gave his unwavering support to the project. 他对这个项目给予了坚定的支持。

notes.en: star power (n.) means the ability of a famous person to attract people
notes.ctx: star 明星 + power 号召力。作者讽刺川总对自己“明星光环”的顽固迷信。
notes.ex1: The film relies heavily on its star power. 这部电影在很大程度上依赖明星号召力。
notes.ex2: Star power alone cannot win an election. 光靠明星光环是赢不了选举的。

paragraphs.en_html: The <mark class="voc">curse</mark> of American politics is its <mark class="voc">bitter</mark> <mark class="voc">partisanship</mark>. As voters have <mark class="voc">sorted</mark> themselves along racial, educational and geographical lines, the parties have spent less time trying to <mark class="voc">win converts</mark> from the other side and more <mark class="voc">whipping their own supporters into a permanent frenzy</mark>: 70% of Republicans are <mark class="voc">hostile</mark> towards Democrats and more than 80% of Democrats <mark class="voc">return the favour</mark>. The result is a style of politics that <mark class="voc">tugs</mark> public life towards the extremes, punishes <mark class="voc">compromise</mark> and <mark class="voc">puts getting people angry above getting things done</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 美国政治的痼疾，是那种你死我活的党派对立。随着选民按种族、学历与地域，各自抱团、分边而站，两党也变了味——它们越来越少地去争取对手阵营的倒戈者，却越来越多地把自家拥趸，煽动进一种持久的癫狂：七成共和党人对民主党满心敌意，八成以上的民主党人，则把这敌意原样奉还。其结果，是一种将公共生活拖向极端、对妥协施以惩罚、把“激怒民众”置于“办成实事”之上的政治。

notes.en: curse (n.) means a cause of harm or misery, something that brings great trouble or bad luck
notes.ctx: 作者不用 problem、trouble，偏用 curse：美国政治的病不是“能解决的问题”，而是“甩不掉的诅咒”，一个词立起“没救了、自己招来的”味道。
notes.ex1: Debt has been the curse of his life. 债务是他一生的祸根。
notes.ex2: Partisanship has become the curse of modern politics. 党派对立已成为现代政治的祸根。

notes.en: bitter (adj.) means angry and resentful, marked by strong hostility
notes.ctx: 从“苦味”引申出“怨恨、尖刻、你死我活”。bitter partisanship＝咬牙切齿的党派对立；对比 bitter enemy（死敌）、bitter quarrel（吵到翻脸的争吵）。
notes.ex1: The two sides are locked in a bitter dispute. 双方陷入了一场激烈的争吵。
notes.ex2: The two old friends became bitter enemies. 这两位老友成了死敌。

notes.en: partisanship (n.) means strong, often unreasonable support for one political party
notes.zh: 党派性，党同伐异，强烈的党派偏见
notes.ctx: partisan 党徒 + -ship 状态。与 bipartisan（两党的、跨党派的）互为反义，如 bipartisan support（两党都支持）。
notes.ex1: Partisanship has made compromise nearly impossible. 党派对立让妥协几乎成了不可能。
notes.ex2: The bill passed only after bitter partisanship. 这项法案是在激烈的党派争斗之后才通过的。

notes.en: sort oneself into means to divide into groups according to shared characteristics
notes.ctx: sorted themselves along...lines 即“沿着……这些线把自己分了类、归了堆”：按种族、学历、地域三条线分边站。背后是 The Big Sort（大分类）现象。
notes.ex1: Voters have sorted themselves into two hostile camps. 选民们已自行分成了两个敌对阵营。
notes.ex2: Online, people sort themselves into groups of like-minded users. 在网上，人们会把自己归入志同道合的群体。

notes.en: win converts means to persuade people to change their beliefs or allegiance
notes.zh: 赢得皈依者，争取倒戈者
notes.ctx: convert 本是宗教用词（改信者）。作者用宗教的词说政治：政党的活儿本该像传教士一样去“传教”，把对方阵营的人争取过来“改信”。
notes.ex1: The party is trying to win converts among young people. 该党正努力在年轻人中争取新支持者。
notes.ex2: The movement is trying to win converts in rural areas. 这场运动正努力在农村地区争取支持者。

notes.en: whip someone into a frenzy means to excite or arouse people to a state of wild, uncontrolled excitement
notes.ctx: whip 本义“鞭子”，英国议会里的“党鞭”典出打猎时拿鞭子把跑偏的猎狗赶回队里的 whipper-in。两党不出去“传教”，改拿鞭子抽自己人，把自家支持者往“永久癫狂”里赶。
notes.ex1: The tabloids whipped the public into a frenzy. 小报把公众煽动得群情激愤。
notes.ex2: The speaker whipped the crowd into a frenzy. 演讲者把人群煽动得热血沸腾。

notes.en: hostile (adj.) means very unfriendly, showing strong dislike or opposition
notes.ctx: 来自拉丁语 hostis“敌人”，即“像对待敌人一样”。be hostile towards＝对……怀有敌意；七成共和党人对民主党怀有敌意。
notes.ex1: The crowd was openly hostile to the proposal. 人群对这项提议表现出明显的敌意。
notes.ex2: He is openly hostile to the new policy. 他对新政策公开持敌意。

notes.en: return the favour means to do something for someone who has done something for you
notes.zh: 还人情，回报恩惠（此处反讽：以牙还牙）
notes.ctx: 作者故意用这个“感恩”的短语去说“还恨”：前面共和党恨民主党，后面民主党“回报”了那份恨。本应还恩，这里却还恨。
notes.ex1: She helped me, so I returned the favour. 她帮过我，所以我也回报了她。
notes.ex2: They supported us last time, so now we should return the favour. 上次他们支持了我们，所以现在我们应该回报他们。

notes.en: tug (v.) means to pull something hard and quickly, especially with a sudden movement
notes.ctx: 画面即 tug of war（拔河）。作者把政治写成拔河里的那只手——它抓住公共生活，使劲往“极端”方向拽，与后面 punish、put 并列，把“政治在主动使坏”写活了。
notes.ex1: The two sides are in a tug of war over the budget. 双方在预算问题上僵持不下。
notes.ex2: The child tugged at her mother’s sleeve. 孩子拽了拽妈妈的袖子。

notes.en: compromise (n.) means an agreement reached by each side giving up something they want in order to end a disagreement
notes.ctx: com- 共同 + promittere 承诺，双方各让一步达成的协议。但作者说美国政治 punishes compromise——惩罚妥协：谁胆敢跟对面握手、各让一步，谁就被自己人收拾、被骂“叛徒”。
notes.ex1: Both sides refused to compromise on the issue. 双方都拒绝在这一问题上妥协。
notes.ex2: After hours of talks, they finally reached a compromise. 经过数小时谈判，他们终于达成了妥协。

notes.en: put A above B means to treat A as more important than B
notes.zh: 把 A 放在 B 之上，重 A 轻 B
notes.ctx: A 是 getting people angry（把人搞愤怒），B 是 getting things done（把事办成）——“让人愤怒”的优先级高于“把事办成”，两个动名词短语作宾语，结构工整。
notes.ex1: He puts profit above everything else. 他把利润看得比什么都重。
notes.ex2: Good leaders put the public interest above their own. 好的领导者把公共利益置于个人利益之上。

paragraphs.en_html: Hispanic and Asian-American voters offer the best hope of <mark class="voc">arresting</mark> this <mark class="voc">baleful</mark> trend. They have become America’s crucial swing voters, with an <mark class="voc">outsize</mark> impact on races across the country. Compared with other <mark class="voc">blocs</mark>, their numbers are growing faster, their ideology is more <mark class="voc">fluid</mark> and their priorities are less <mark class="voc">divisive</mark>. That means they are likely to be good for America not just in these midterms, but also for many elections to come.
paragraphs.zh: 拉美裔和亚裔选民，是遏制这股不祥趋势的最大希望。他们已然成为美国举足轻重的摇摆选民，对全国各地的选战，有着远超其人数规模的影响力。相较其他阵营，他们的人数增长更快，立场更流动、更不固化，最关切的议题也没那么撕裂。这意味着，他们很可能成为美国的福音——不仅在此次中期选举，更在此后一场又一场的选战里。

notes.en: arrest (v.) means to stop or check the progress or development of something
notes.ctx: 陷阱词，跟“逮捕”无关。arrest 的核心义永远是“停”：cardiac arrest 心脏骤停、arrested development 发育停滞、arrest the decline 遏制下滑。arresting this baleful trend＝让这股趋势停下来。
notes.ex1: The government moved to arrest the decline in manufacturing. 政府出手遏制制造业的下滑。
notes.ex2: Doctors could not arrest the spread of the disease. 医生们无法阻止这种疾病的蔓延。

notes.en: baleful (adj.) means threatening harm, ominous, evil
notes.ctx: 古英语 bealu“灾祸、邪恶”，弥尔顿《失乐园》有 baleful eyes（邪恶之眼）。不说 bad trend，偏说 baleful trend，那股“带着邪气、会招来祸事”的味道全出来了，与第 2 段的 curse 同一语域。
notes.ex1: The baleful influence of extremism has spread. 极端主义那有害的影响已经蔓延开来。
notes.ex2: The policy has had a baleful effect on the economy. 这项政策对经济产生了有害的影响。

notes.en: outsize (adj.) means larger than normal, disproportionately great
notes.zh: 超出常规的，不成比例地大的
notes.ctx: out 超出 + size 尺寸。outsize impact＝影响力超出了它的人数规模——人不多，劲儿特别大，背后是“赢者通吃 + 摇摆州”机制。
notes.ex1: A few states have an outsize impact on the result. 少数几个州对选举结果有不成比例的影响。
notes.ex2: Big donors have an outsize voice in the party. 大额捐款人在党内拥有不成比例的话语权。

notes.en: bloc (n.) means a group of countries or people with shared interests who vote together
notes.ctx: 注意是 bloc，没有 k，别写成 block（街区、块）。other blocs＝其他选民阵营（白人、黑人、其他族裔等）。
notes.ex1: The youth bloc could decide this election. 青年阵营可能决定这场选举的走向。
notes.ex2: Women now form an important voting bloc. 女性如今构成一个重要的选民阵营。

notes.en: fluid (adj.) means likely to change, not fixed or settled
notes.ctx: 水没有固定形状，倒进圆的杯子就是圆的、倒进方的就是方的。their ideology is more fluid＝意识形态没定型，与别人“已经凝固成铁板”的立场形成对比，与标题 dynamic、swing 一条线。
notes.ex1: The political situation remains fluid. 政治局势依然变化不定。
notes.ex2: The candidate’s positions remain fluid on several issues. 这位候选人在几个问题上的立场仍不固定。

notes.en: divisive (adj.) means causing disagreement or hostility between people
notes.ctx: divide 分裂 + -ive。less divisive＝没那么撕裂：他们最关心的事，不是那种一谈起来就让人翻脸、把人劈成两半的议题——言下之意，跟他们是可以坐下来谈的。
notes.ex1: Immigration is a deeply divisive issue. 移民是一个极具分裂性的议题。
notes.ex2: The leader avoided divisive topics during the campaign. 这位领导人在竞选期间避开了撕裂性的议题。

paragraphs.en_html: No group <mark class="voc">captures the potential</mark> for opening up politics as much as Hispanics and Asian-Americans. One reason is <mark class="voc">demography</mark>. They are a growing <mark class="voc">fraction</mark> of the population—especially Hispanics, who are three times more numerous than Asian-Americans. Since 2006 their combined share of the <mark class="voc">electorate</mark> has increased by nine percentage points, to reach 21%. They are also highly <mark class="voc">diverse</mark>. The grandchildren of an immigrant from Ho Chi Minh City have a different outlook from a new arrival from Bangalore. Neither fits neatly into the familiar Democrat-Republican <mark class="voc">template</mark>. And they are more likely to switch their votes. In 2012 Democrats thought they <mark class="voc">had a lock on</mark> Latinos and Asians. In 2024 the story was how they were becoming <mark class="voc">Trumpian</mark>. It has now become clear that they were swing voters <mark class="voc">all along</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 没有任何一个群体，能像拉美裔和亚裔这样，牢牢抓住“让政治重新打开”的潜力。原因之一是人口——他们在总人口中的占比不断攀升，尤其是拉美裔，人数是亚裔的三倍有余。自 2006 年以来，两者合计在选民中的占比已上升 9 个百分点，达到 21%。同时，他们也极为多元：一位胡志明市移民的孙辈，与一位刚从班加罗尔落脚的新移民，对世界的看法截然不同；而这两者，谁也无法被整齐地塞进那套熟悉的“民主党—共和党”模板。此外，他们也更可能改换选票。2012 年，民主党人还笃定自己已把拉美裔和亚裔牢牢攥在手里；到了 2024 年，故事却成了他们日渐“特朗普化”；而如今，真相已然明了——他们从头到尾，就是摇摆选民。

notes.en: capture the potential means to succeed in realising or taking hold of a possibility
notes.ctx: capture 本义捕捉、抓拍——一个瞬间按下快门把它“捕捉”下来。作者说这群人“抓住了让政治重新打开”的潜力，是本段的“纲”。
notes.ex1: The company failed to capture the potential of the new market. 这家公司未能抓住新市场的潜力。
notes.ex2: The photograph captures the energy of the moment. 这张照片捕捉到了那一刻的活力。

notes.en: demography (n.) means the study of populations, their size, structure and distribution
notes.ctx: demo- 来自希腊语 demos“人民”（与 democracy 同源）+ -graphy 写、记。作者给出的第一个理由：人口结构。
notes.ex1: Demography helps explain the country’s shifting politics. 人口学有助于解释这个国家政治格局的变化。
notes.ex2: Rapid demographic change is reshaping many cities. 快速的人口结构变化正在重塑许多城市。

notes.en: fraction (n.) means a small part or proportion of something
notes.ctx: 来自拉丁语 frangere 打碎，即“被掰下来的一块”。a growing fraction of the population＝总人口中占比越来越大的一部分。
notes.ex1: They represent a growing fraction of the electorate. 他们在选民中的占比越来越大。
notes.ex2: Only a fraction of voters turned out. 只有一小部分选民出来投票。

notes.en: the electorate (n.) means all the people who are entitled to vote in an election
notes.ctx: elect 选举 + -orate 群体。their combined share of the electorate＝两者合计在全体选民中的占比。
notes.ex1: The candidates spent months trying to win over the electorate. 候选人们花了几个月时间争取全体选民。
notes.ex2: The electorate has grown younger and more diverse. 选民群体变得更年轻、更多元。

notes.en: diverse (adj.) means showing a great deal of variety, very different from each other
notes.ctx: di- 分开 + vers 转，即“朝不同方向转开”。作者说的“多元”不是“他们跟别人不一样”，而是“他们内部自己跟自己就不一样”。
notes.ex1: The team is highly diverse in terms of background. 这支队伍在背景上非常多元。
notes.ex2: A diverse society needs flexible politics. 多元的社会需要灵活的政治。

notes.en: template (n.) means a pattern or model used as a guide for making things
notes.zh: 模板，模子；固定的分类框架
notes.ctx: 工厂里那个固定的模子，东西倒进去出来一个固定形状。the Democrat-Republican template＝非黑即白的党派分类框；fits neatly into 即“整整齐齐套进去”，这两人塞不进这个框。
notes.ex1: The report can serve as a template for future work. 这份报告可以作为今后工作的模板。
notes.ex2: These voters don’t fit into any simple template. 这些选民套不进任何简单的模板。

notes.en: have a lock on something means to have complete control of something, to be sure of winning it
notes.ctx: 给某样东西上把锁。特别口语化的政治表达：2012 年民主党以为拉美裔和亚裔“锁死了、稳了、铁定投我们”，结果大错特错。
notes.ex1: The team seems to have a lock on the championship. 这支队伍似乎已经锁定了冠军。
notes.ex2: The party once thought it had a lock on the youth vote. 该党一度以为自己稳拿青年选票。

notes.en: Trumpian (adj.) means in the style of or characteristic of Donald Trump
notes.zh: 特朗普式的，特朗普化的
notes.ctx: 人名 + -ian 构成形容词，如 Orwellian 奥威尔式的、Shakespearean 莎士比亚式的——把一个“人”变成一种“风格”。they were becoming Trumpian＝他们正变得民粹、反建制、语不惊人死不休。
notes.ex1: The speech had a distinctly Trumpian tone. 那篇演讲带着明显的特朗普腔。
notes.ex2: His opponents called the policy dangerously Trumpian. 他的对手称这项政策是危险的特朗普式的。

notes.en: all along means from the very beginning, the whole time
notes.ctx: 全文情绪最猛的一句：他们不是“变心了”，是“本来就没固定过”。all along 把“从头到尾”这个真相狠狠砸在脸上——不是你今天才发现他们摇摆，是你今天才肯承认。
notes.ex1: I knew it all along. 我打一开始就知道。
notes.ex2: He had been right all along. 他一直都是对的。

paragraphs.en_html: White voters changed little between 2020 and 2024, while both Latinos and Asians <mark class="voc">lurched</mark> hard to the right. They were then the fastest to turn against Mr Trump in early 2025. The <mark class="voc">margin of support</mark> for Democrats has risen by 17 points among Latinos and 14 among Asians since 2024, compared with ten for whites and five for black voters.
paragraphs.zh: 从 2020 到 2024 年，白人选民几乎纹丝未动，拉美裔和亚裔却猛地向右栽去。而到了 2025 年初，他们又成了全美最快掉头、转而反对特朗普的群体。自 2024 年以来，民主党在拉美裔中的支持优势上升了 17 个点，在亚裔中上升了 14 个点；相形之下，白人仅上升 10 个点，黑人选民更是只有 5 个点。

notes.en: lurch (v.) means to move suddenly and unsteadily, especially to one side, to stagger
notes.ctx: 1784 年才进英语的航海词：大浪里船突然往一边猛地一歪。lurch 跟 swing 完全不是一回事：swing 是秋千来回荡（荡过去还能荡回来），lurch 是栽（幅度大、猛、突然，甚至带“要翻车”的危险感）。lurched hard to the right＝狠狠地向右栽了过去。
notes.ex1: The car lurched to one side. 汽车猛地向一侧倾斜。
notes.ex2: The economy lurched from one crisis to another. 经济从一个危机踉跄跌入另一个危机。

notes.en: margin of support means the difference between the level of support for one side and the other, the lead
notes.ctx: margin 本义边缘、页边空白，引申为“两个数之间的差”。数据新闻最容易搞混的词：margin 不是“支持率本身”，而是“支持民主党的比支持共和党的多多少”——那个领先的差额。
notes.ex1: The party won by a narrow margin. 该党以微弱优势获胜。
notes.ex2: The poll shows a razor-thin margin of support for the president. 民调显示总统的支持优势微乎其微。

paragraphs.en_html: Part of the explanation for this is that these voters are the <mark class="voc">epitome</mark> of <mark class="voc">striving</mark> Americans who want to work hard and <mark class="voc">get ahead</mark>. Higher prices for food and fuel <mark class="voc">hit Hispanic voters particularly hard</mark>; housing costs affected Asian voters. Latinos are more than twice as likely to start businesses as white voters. Asians are likely to spend more time in education.
paragraphs.zh: 出现这种现象，部分原因在于：这些选民，正是“奋斗的美国人”的缩影——他们渴望辛勤工作、出人头地。食品与燃油的涨价，对拉美裔选民的打击尤重；住房成本，则沉甸甸地压在亚裔头上。拉美裔创业的可能性，是白人选民的两倍有余；而亚裔，则更倾向于把更多时间投进教育。

notes.en: epitome (n.) means a person or thing that is a perfect example of a particular quality or type
notes.ctx: 希腊语 epitemnein“剪短、切下来”，与 anatomy 解剖、atom 原子同属“切”字根家族。读音陷阱：重音在第二个音节，末 e 读“me”。这些选民是“奋斗的美国人的缩影”——想了解典型美国奋斗者，看他们就行。
notes.ex1: She is the epitome of a hard worker. 她是勤奋者的典型代表。
notes.ex2: That neighbourhood is the epitome of the American dream. 那个社区就是美国梦的缩影。

notes.en: striving (adj.) means making great efforts to achieve something
notes.ctx: 动词 strive 努力、奋斗的现在分词作形容词。striving Americans＝正在努力往上爬的美国人。
notes.ex1: The city is full of striving young families. 这座城市满是努力打拼的年轻家庭。
notes.ex2: She grew up in a striving immigrant household. 她在一个努力奋斗的移民家庭长大。

notes.en: get ahead means to be successful in your career or life, to make progress
notes.ctx: ahead 在前面，get ahead 即“跑到前面去”。特别口语化、特别“美国梦”的表达——努力工作，然后出人头地。
notes.ex1: He works hard to get ahead. 他努力工作以求上进。
notes.ex2: In this town, working hard is how you get ahead. 在这个镇上，努力工作是出人头地的途径。

notes.en: hit someone hard means to affect someone severely, to cause great difficulty
notes.ctx: 本义“狠狠地打了某人一下”，用在物价、灾难上即“重创”。为什么拉美裔特别疼？食品和燃油全是“过日子”的刚需，物价一涨，他们的钱包最先疼。
notes.ex1: The recession hit small businesses hard. 经济衰退对小企业打击沉重。
notes.ex2: Rising rents have hit young families hard. 不断上涨的房租让年轻家庭苦不堪言。

paragraphs.en_html: Many are <mark class="voc">recent arrivals</mark> or the children of immigrants, so their opinions have not yet <mark class="voc">hardened</mark> along party lines. In contrast to the rest of the voting population, if Hispanics and Asians hold one <mark class="voc">left-leaning</mark> position, they will not necessarily <mark class="voc">endorse</mark> others. Likewise, wanting a secure southern border does not <mark class="voc">equate to</mark> support for the <mark class="voc">hardline</mark> enforcement that has frightened Hispanic employees into staying away from work.
paragraphs.zh: 他们中的许多人，是刚来不久的新移民，或移民的子女，其政治观点因而尚未在党派界限上固化。与其余选民群体不同，拉美裔与亚裔即便在某一议题上持偏左立场，也未必会连带支持其他偏左主张。同样地，“希望拥有一条安全的南部边境”，并不等同于“支持那种强硬执法”——正是这种执法，已把拉美裔员工吓得不敢出门上班。

notes.en: recent arrivals means people who have just arrived, newly arrived immigrants
notes.ctx: arrival 到达，此处指人——刚刚落脚的新移民。点出这群人的出身：他们要么自己刚来，要么爸妈刚来，都是“新美国人的头两代”。
notes.ex1: The school welcomes recent arrivals from many countries. 这所学校欢迎来自许多国家的新移民。
notes.ex2: Recent arrivals often start with low-paying jobs. 新移民往往从低收入工作做起。

notes.en: harden (v.) means to become or make something firm, solid or fixed
notes.ctx: hard 硬 + -en 使变……。观点“还没变硬”＝还像橡皮泥一样软、可塑。与第 3 段 fluid 一条线——软 vs 硬、流动 vs 僵化。党派认同靠父母传承，移民这一环“断档”，所以要好几代才慢慢“硬”起来。
notes.ex1: Opinions have hardened on both sides. 双方的态度都已变得强硬。
notes.ex2: As the campaign went on, their positions hardened. 随着竞选推进，他们的立场变得强硬起来。

notes.en: left-leaning (adj.) means tending to support left-wing or progressive political views
notes.ctx: left 左 + leaning 倾向。政治上“左”一般指支持进步、大政府、平等、多元；“右”指保守、小政府、传统。
notes.ex1: The newspaper is known for its left-leaning editorials. 这家报纸以左倾的社论闻名。
notes.ex2: He comes from a left-leaning family. 他出身于一个偏左的家庭。

notes.en: endorse (v.) means to publicly say that you support or approve of someone or something
notes.ctx: en- 在……上 + dorse 背（拉丁语 dorsum 背部），本指在支票背面签字即“背书”。这群人不会因为在一个点上偏左，就自动“背书”其他所有偏左的东西——立场是“散装”的，不是“打包”的。
notes.ex1: The newspaper endorsed the incumbent. 这家报纸为现任者背书。
notes.ex2: The union endorsed the governor for re-election. 工会为州长连任背书。

notes.en: equate to means to be equal to, to be the same as
notes.ctx: 来自拉丁语 aequare“使相等”，与 equal 同族。does not equate to＝不等于、不能画等号：别把“要边境安全”和“支持强硬执法”两件事混为一谈。
notes.ex1: Higher spending does not always equate to better results. 更高的投入并不总等于更好的结果。
notes.ex2: Wanting border security does not equate to opposing immigration. 想要边境安全并不等于反对移民。

notes.en: hardline (adj.) means strict and uncompromising, refusing to change
notes.ctx: hard 硬 + line 线，立场强硬、寸步不让。hardline enforcement＝强硬执法——那种雷厉风行、不留情面的打击。
notes.ex1: He has taken a hardline stance on crime. 他在犯罪问题上采取了强硬立场。
notes.ex2: Hardliners within the party oppose any compromise. 党内的强硬派反对任何妥协。

paragraphs.en_html: Instead, many are <mark class="voc">moderate</mark>. They <mark class="voc">have little truck with</mark> <mark class="voc">culture wars</mark> or <mark class="voc">polarisation</mark>. The economic policies they care about <mark class="voc">diverge from</mark> the <mark class="voc">tribal</mark> messages the parties use to <mark class="voc">stir up</mark> their <mark class="voc">bases</mark>. Whereas policies on abortion and trans rights are <mark class="voc">set at the extremes</mark>, economic management is suited to the swing voter’s <mark class="voc">pragmatic</mark> preference for <mark class="voc">the common good</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 恰恰相反，他们中的许多人，是温和派。他们对“文化战争”、对“极化”这类事，几乎不屑于沾边。他们真正关心的经济政策，与两党用来煽动各自基本盘的部落式口号，本就背道而驰。堕胎、跨性别权利等议题，天然被钉死在两个极端；而经济治理，才真正契合摇摆选民那种务实、且着眼于公共利益的偏好。

notes.en: moderate (adj.) means neither extreme nor excessive, keeping within reasonable limits
notes.ctx: 拉丁语 moderatus“有节制的”，词根 modus“尺度、分寸”（即 mode、model 里的 mod）。作者给这群人定调：他们不是“没立场”，是“不极端”。
notes.ex1: She holds moderate views on most issues. 她在大多数问题上持温和立场。
notes.ex2: Most voters want moderate, practical solutions. 大多数选民想要温和、务实的解决方案。

notes.en: have no truck with someone or something means to refuse to have anything to do with them, to avoid dealing with them
notes.ctx: truck 不是卡车，是法语 troquer“以物易物、交易”；truck“交易”引申出“往来、打交道”。这个短语天生带着“我不跟你做这笔肮脏交易”的味儿。
notes.ex1: I’ll have no truck with that kind of behaviour. 我绝不跟那种行为沾边。
notes.ex2: I have little truck with people who spread rumours. 我不屑于跟散布谣言的人打交道。

notes.en: culture wars (n.) means conflicts between groups with different values, especially over social issues
notes.ctx: 从德语 Kulturkampf 借来，1992 年共和党人布坎南在党代会上喊火。不是打“钱怎么分”，是打“价值观谁说了算”——堕胎、跨性别、枪支这些“你信什么”的议题，与物价、工资这类“面包黄油议题”相对。
notes.ex1: The party is fighting a culture war over schools. 该党正围绕学校打一场文化战争。
notes.ex2: The country has been trapped in culture wars for years. 这个国家多年来一直深陷文化战争。

notes.en: polarisation (n.) means the process of dividing into two sharply contrasting groups
notes.ctx: polar 极 + -isation……化：整个社会往两个极端跑、中间空掉。英式拼写用 s，美式 polarization 用 z。
notes.ex1: Political polarisation makes governing harder. 政治两极分化让治理更加困难。
notes.ex2: The country has seen growing polarisation over the past decade. 过去十年，这个国家的两极分化不断加剧。

notes.en: diverge from means to go in a different direction, to differ from
notes.ctx: di- 分开 + verge 转，“往两个方向岔开”；反义 converge 汇合。他们关心的经济政策，跟两党那个“部落化口号”是岔开的、不是一路的。
notes.ex1: Their interests diverge from those of the party. 他们的利益与该党背道而驰。
notes.ex2: His views diverge from those of his party. 他的观点与党内其他人不同。

notes.en: tribal (adj.) means relating to a tribe, showing strong loyalty to one’s own group
notes.zh: 部落的；只忠于自己人的
notes.ctx: 原始部落什么样？自己人抱团、外人全是敌人。tribal messages＝只喊给自家人听、把外人当敌人的口号，与第 2 段“两党只煽动自己人”呼应。
notes.ex1: The debate descended into tribal shouting. 辩论沦为部落式的叫骂。
notes.ex2: Tribal loyalties now drive most voting decisions. 如今大多数投票决定由圈子忠诚驱动。

notes.en: stir up means to cause strong feelings, to excite or provoke
notes.ctx: stir 搅拌——搅一锅粥。stir up their bases＝把自家死忠粉的情绪搅起来，与第 2 段 whip into a frenzy 是同义的换着花样骂。
notes.ex1: The speech stirred up old resentments. 那番话挑起了旧日的怨恨。
notes.ex2: He tried to stir up anger among his supporters. 他试图煽动支持者的怒火。

notes.en: base (n.) means a group of people who reliably support a political party
notes.ctx: base 基础，引申为“一个党最死忠的那群支持者”。stir up their bases＝煽动基本盘。
notes.ex1: The candidate focused on energising the party’s base. 这位候选人专注于动员基本盘。
notes.ex2: The party’s base is older and more conservative. 这个党的基本盘年纪更大、更保守。

notes.en: set at the extremes means fixed at the two opposite ends of a range
notes.ctx: 堕胎、跨性别这种议题，天生“站两头”——你不可能“堕胎堕一半”，也不可能“跨性别跨一半”，一谈就炸、一碰就撕。
notes.ex1: On abortion, opinions are set at the extremes. 在堕胎问题上，观点往往极端对立。
notes.ex2: The two parties are set at opposite extremes on this issue. 在这个问题上，两党立场极端对立。

notes.en: pragmatic (adj.) means dealing with problems in a practical way rather than by following fixed ideas or theories
notes.ctx: 希腊语 pragma“事情、行动、实践”，核心是“看实际效果、别整虚的”。一个 pragmatic 的人，不问“这事符不符合我的理念”，只问“这事管不管用”。
notes.ex1: She takes a pragmatic approach to problems. 她处理问题讲究务实。
notes.ex2: We need a pragmatic solution that actually works. 我们需要一个真正管用的务实方案。

notes.en: the common good means the benefit or interests of all people in society
notes.ctx: common 共同 + good 好处。点睛之笔：两党的部落化口号全是为“自己人”，而这群温和选民偏好的是 the common good——“大家共同的好”。
notes.ex1: Leaders should work for the common good. 领导者应当为公共利益服务。
notes.ex2: Sometimes individual interests must yield to the common good. 有时个人利益必须让位于公共利益。

paragraphs.en_html: Almost anything that gives the parties a reason to <mark class="voc">appeal to</mark> the centre will benefit America, especially when it involves the <mark class="voc">virtues</mark> of hard work and prosperity. Democrats will need a winning economic message and a <mark class="voc">coherent</mark> plan for immigration. Republicans should <mark class="voc">reject</mark> their <mark class="voc">ferocious</mark> <mark class="voc">deportations</mark> and the ugly <mark class="voc">ultranationalism</mark> that <mark class="voc">denigrates</mark> Hispanic and Asian citizens for not being “<mark class="voc">heritage Americans</mark>”.
paragraphs.zh: 几乎任何能让两党有理由去争取中间选民的东西，都会让美国受益——尤其当它关乎“勤奋”与“繁荣”这些美德的时候。民主党，需要一套能打动人心的经济叙事，以及一个前后自洽的移民方案。共和党，则应当摒弃他们那凶残的驱逐，以及那丑恶的极端民族主义——正是这种民族主义，以“血统”为尺，诋毁拉美裔与亚裔公民，称他们不配做所谓的“血统美国人”。

notes.en: appeal to someone means to attract or interest them, to be pleasing to them
notes.ctx: appeal 本义呼吁、恳求，appeal to sb 另有“吸引某人、迎合某人心意”的常用义。appeal to the centre＝去争取中间派，背后是“中间选民定理”：谁贴近中间谁就赢。
notes.ex1: This policy appeals to middle-class voters. 这项政策对中产阶级选民很有吸引力。
notes.ex2: The candidate is trying to appeal to working-class voters. 这位候选人正努力争取工薪阶层选民。

notes.en: virtues (n.) means good qualities or moral standards
notes.ctx: the virtues of hard work and prosperity＝勤奋与繁荣这些美德，呼应第 6 段“奋斗者”人设——争的是“把日子过好”，不是争“谁更配当美国人”。
notes.ex1: Hard work and honesty are old-fashioned virtues. 勤奋与诚实是老派的传统美德。
notes.ex2: The campaign celebrates the virtues of hard work. 这场竞选颂扬勤奋的美德。

notes.en: coherent (adj.) means logical, well-organised, consistent
notes.zh: 连贯的，前后一致的，逻辑自洽的
notes.ctx: co- 共同 + her 粘（拉丁语 haerere 粘住），即“粘在一起、没散架”。作者措辞很毒：潜台词是民主党现在的移民方案是 incoherent 的——乱的、自相矛盾的。
notes.ex1: They lack a coherent strategy. 他们缺乏一套连贯的战略。
notes.ex2: The party still lacks a coherent immigration plan. 该党仍缺乏一个前后一致的移民方案。

notes.en: reject (v.) means to refuse to accept or support something
notes.ctx: re- 回 + ject 抛，即“抛回去、不接受”。Republicans should reject their ferocious deportations——共和党应该抛弃他们的凶残驱逐。
notes.ex1: The committee rejected the proposal. 委员会否决了这项提议。
notes.ex2: He rejected calls to step down. 他拒绝了要求他下台的呼声。

notes.en: ferocious (adj.) means fierce, violent and savage
notes.ctx: 词根拉丁语 ferox“野的、凶猛的”，用来形容野兽。作者不说 strict（严格）或 tough（强硬），偏说 ferocious——这一个词，立场全露出来了：他不只反对“驱逐”这个政策，是说这政策“残忍到没人性”。
notes.ex1: The storm was ferocious. 那场暴风雨来势凶猛。
notes.ex2: The two candidates engaged in a ferocious debate. 两位候选人展开了一场激烈的辩论。

notes.en: deportation (n.) means the act of forcing someone to leave a country, especially because they have no legal right to stay
notes.ctx: de- 离开 + port 运送，即“把人送走”。特朗普第二任期的头号工程，作者用 ferocious（凶残）来形容它。
notes.ex1: Thousands of families now face deportation. 成千上万的家庭如今面临被驱逐出境。
notes.ex2: The policy calls for the mass deportation of undocumented immigrants. 这项政策要求大规模驱逐无证移民。

notes.en: ultranationalism (n.) means extreme nationalism, the belief that one’s own nation is superior to all others
notes.ctx: ultra- 极端的（如 ultraviolet 紫外线）+ nationalism 民族主义，即走火入魔的民族主义。作者用 ugly（丑恶的）修饰它——不只是“错误的”，更是“丑的、见不得人的”。
notes.ex1: Rising ultranationalism worries many observers. 日益高涨的极端民族主义令许多观察者担忧。
notes.ex2: The leader’s rhetoric slid into ultranationalism. 这位领导人的言论滑向了极端民族主义。

notes.en: denigrate (v.) means to criticise or say bad things about someone in a way that is unfair
notes.ctx: de- 向下 + nigr 黑（拉丁语 niger 黑色），字面即“把……涂黑”，与中文“抹黑”是同一个逻辑。想表达“污名化、泼脏水”，denigrate 比 criticise 高级多了。
notes.ex1: The campaign denigrated its opponents. 这场竞选抹黑了对手。
notes.ex2: He constantly denigrates his rivals. 他不断贬损自己的对手。

notes.en: heritage Americans means, in nativist rhetoric, Americans whose ancestry can be traced back to the founding of the country
notes.ctx: heritage 血统、传承，即“祖辈能一路追溯到美国建国初期的人”，说白了就是早期盎格鲁-撒克逊白人移民的后代。右翼 MAGA 圈的新词，是“白人至上”的马甲；作者加引号是“撇清、讽刺”——引号有时就是作者在翻白眼。
notes.ex1: Some on the far right claim to speak for so-called ‘heritage Americans’. 极右翼的一些人自称代表所谓的“血统美国人”。
notes.ex2: The term ‘heritage Americans’ is a euphemism for racial exclusion. “血统美国人”这个说法是种族排外的委婉语。

paragraphs.en_html: All Americans should therefore welcome these new swing voters. <mark class="voc">Thanks to</mark> them, fewer elections will be decided by <mark class="voc">hard-core</mark> party members in <mark class="voc">primaries</mark>, and more by the average voter in the <mark class="voc">general election</mark>. If politicians <mark class="voc">win more credit</mark> by accomplishing something in government, they will perhaps spend less of their time <mark class="voc">demonising</mark> the other side. If the economy seems to matter more and culture wars less, America will be more <mark class="voc">prosperous</mark> and better governed. Hispanic and Asian immigrants want the chance to <mark class="voc">thrive</mark>. Their votes will help ensure America thrives with them.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，所有美国人都应当欢迎这些新的摇摆选民。多亏了他们，会有更少的选举由初选里的铁杆党员说了算，而更多的选举，交由大选中的普通选民来定夺。倘若政客能靠在政府里成就实事来赢得赞誉，他们兴许就会少花些时间去妖魔化对手。倘若经济变得更重要、文化战争变得次要，美国就将更繁荣，也治理得更好。拉美裔与亚裔移民，渴望的是一个能够“兴旺”的机会；而他们的选票，将有助于确保——美国，与他们一同兴旺。

notes.en: thanks to means because of, as a result of
notes.ctx: 可褒可贬：既可是“幸亏”，也可带反讽“拜……所赐”。Thanks to them＝多亏了他们。
notes.ex1: Thanks to their hard work, the project succeeded. 多亏他们的努力，项目成功了。
notes.ex2: Thanks to the new system, voting is now easier. 多亏了新系统，投票现在更容易了。

notes.en: hard-core (adj.) means extremely committed, the most dedicated and uncompromising members
notes.ctx: 本为地质学、建筑学词“硬核”，引申为最核心、最死忠、最狂热的那一小撮。hard-core party members＝把党派当信仰、死忠到底的人。
notes.ex1: The hard-core fans never miss a match. 铁杆球迷从不缺席比赛。
notes.ex2: Only hard-core party members turn out for the primaries. 只有铁杆党员才会参加初选。

notes.en: primaries (n.) means elections in which a party chooses its candidate for a main election
notes.ctx: 大选前各党在党内选“谁代表本党出战”的环节。美国政治的“暗门”：初选投票率极低（平均仅 15%–25%），参加者多是意识形态最极端、最狂热的铁杆，所以初选选出的候选人往往比中间选民极端得多。
notes.ex1: The primaries attracted only the most committed voters. 初选只吸引了最死忠的那批选民。
notes.ex2: Candidates must first win their party’s primary before the general election. 候选人必须先赢得本党初选，才能进入大选。

notes.en: a general election means a national election in which voters choose their representatives
notes.ctx: 与初选 primary 相对的、全民参与的正式选举。作者的意思是：把“谁当政”的决定权，从那 20% 极端铁杆手里，交还给大多数普通老百姓。
notes.ex1: The general election will be held in November. 大选将于十一月举行。
notes.ex2: Turnout is much higher in the general election than in the primaries. 大选的投票率远高于初选。

notes.en: win credit for means to earn praise or recognition for doing something
notes.ctx: credit 此处指“功劳、赞誉、认可”。潜台词：政客现在不靠“做事”赢好评，靠“骂人”。
notes.ex1: She won credit for fixing the budget. 她因修复预算而赢得赞誉。
notes.ex2: Politicians should win credit for getting things done, not for attacking rivals. 政客应当靠做事赢得赞誉，而不是靠攻击对手。

notes.en: demonise (v.) means to describe someone or something as very bad or dangerous, often unfairly
notes.ctx: demon 恶魔 + -ise 使……化。政客发现骂人更省事：只要把对面党妖魔化成恶魔，告诉你“对面一上台你就完蛋”，你自然就投我了。英式拼写 demonise，美式 demonize。
notes.ex1: The media demonised the protesters. 媒体把抗议者妖魔化了。
notes.ex2: Each side tries to demonise the other during elections. 选举期间，各方都试图把对方妖魔化。

notes.en: prosperous (adj.) means successful and rich, thriving
notes.ctx: 与 prosperity 同根。more prosperous and better governed＝更繁荣、治理得更好。
notes.ex1: The city became more prosperous under the new policies. 在新政策下，这座城市变得更加繁荣。
notes.ex2: A prosperous country invests in its people. 繁荣的国家会投资于自己的人民。

notes.en: thrive (v.) means to grow, develop and become successful, to flourish
notes.ctx: 词源古诺尔斯语 þrífask，本义“抓住、紧紧攥给自己”——兴旺不是被施舍，而是自己伸手抓住机会。全文点睛：immigrants thrive 升华到 America thrives，与标题 changing for the better 首尾呼应。
notes.ex1: The business thrived under her leadership. 这家企业在她领导下兴旺起来。
notes.ex2: Small businesses thrive when the economy is stable. 经济稳定时，小企业就能蓬勃发展。

proper.name: midterm elections / 中期选举
proper.def:
美国政治制度的一部分：总统四年一选，但众议员两年一选、参议员六年一选，所以总统干满两年会撞上一场全国性的国会选举，俗称对总统的“期中考试”。2026 年这场：众议院 435 席全换、参议院改选 35 席；共和党虽“一手抓”（白宫＋两院），但全是险胜——众议院 218 对 214、参议院 53 对 47，民主党多赢几席即翻盘。另有一个“中期选举魔咒”：总统所在的党几乎次次丢国会席位（二战以来仅个别例外，如 2002 年小布什）。
本文中的意思：全文的时间坐标。作者说中期选举是“对总统的公投”，不是修辞——老百姓真把这场选举当成给总统打分的卷子。

proper.name: Electoral College / winner-take-all 选举人团与赢者通吃
proper.def:
美国大选不直接数人头，而是“选举人团制”，且多数州实行“赢者通吃”：你在一个州比对手多一张票，这个州的全部选举人票就全归你——多一票和多一百万票结果一样。2016 年希拉里在全国普选票比特朗普多 200 多万张，却因特朗普在威斯康星（赢 2.2 万票）、密歇根（赢 1 万票）、宾夕法尼亚（赢 4.4 万票）几个关键摇摆州毫厘之差全拿，最终输掉大选。有学者估算，总统选举结果有时掌握在 15 万到 20 万个摇摆选民手里。
本文中的意思：解释了第 3 段 outsize impact 为什么成立——人不在多，在关键位置。拉美裔和亚裔是摇摆选民，一旦移动一点点，在势均力敌的州里就能翻转整个州、进而翻转整个国家。

proper.name: swing state / 摇摆州
proper.def:
美国五十州大多“锁死”：加州、纽约铁投民主党，得州、阿拉巴马铁投共和党。真正拼刺刀的是五六个摇摆州——宾夕法尼亚、密歇根、威斯康星、亚利桑那等，今天可能投蓝、明天投红。选举年候选人天天往这几个州跑、撒广告。
本文中的意思：与 swing voter 是一套逻辑。作者说拉美裔和亚裔是 most dynamic swing voters，就是在说他们是美国政治里最像“摇摆州”的那个变量，最值得两党去抢。

proper.name: Pew Research Center / 皮尤研究中心
proper.def:
美国权威民调机构。第 2 段那组“70% 共和党人敌视民主党、80% 以上民主党人回敬”的数据即出自它的测量。政治学给这种现象起名“情感极化”（affective polarization）：不是政策分歧（可以谈），而是情感对立（我恨你这个人、把你当敌人）。学者用“情感温度计”测：0 度冷到极点、100 度热到极点，两党选民给对方打的平均分只有二十几分。另有一个扎心数据：约四成美国人会因孩子嫁给“对面党派”的人而感到不舒服。
本文中的意思：作者第 2 段那组数字不是拍脑袋，是反复测量过的事实。

proper.name: The Big Sort / 《大分类》
proper.def:
2008 年记者比尔·毕晓普（Bill Bishop）与统计学家合写的书。核心观点：过去几十年美国人正“用脚投票”，搬去跟自己观点一样的人住。书中用“压倒性县”（landslide county，一个党赢对手 20 个百分点以上的县）量化：1976 年约四分之一美国人住这种县，2004 年近一半（48%），2016 年冲到 62%。
本文中的意思：第 2 段 sorted themselves along lines 背后的学术出处——这个国家正在自己把自己切成两半。

proper.name: median voter theorem / 中间选民定理
proper.def:
安东尼·唐斯（Anthony Downs）1957 年在《民主的经济理论》中提出：理性的政客为了赢选举，会自动往“中间选民”的位置靠，因为谁靠中间谁就赢。他还说过一句扎心的话：政客“是为了赢选举才去制定政策，而不是为了制定政策才去赢选举”。
本文中的意思：第 9 段 appeal to the centre 背后的政治学规律——只要两党有理由争取中间选民，政治就会自动往中间走，离撕裂远一步。

proper.name: Ho Chi Minh City / 胡志明市（越南）
proper.def:
越南第一大城市，旧称西贡，1975 年越战结束、北越攻入后被改名。南越亲美人士当年纷纷乘小渔船逃亡，那场逃亡史称“投奔怒海”——船小人多、没水没粮，很多人死于海盗与风浪。逃到美国的这批人成了今天的 200 多万越南裔，因是被共产党政权赶出来的，历史上是亚裔里最保守、最亲共和党的一支（2020 年大选是唯一支持特朗普多于拜登的亚裔群体）。
本文中的意思：第 4 段用“胡志明市移民的孙辈”指代一群反共、保守、偏共和党的人的后代。

proper.name: Bangalore / 班加罗尔（印度）
proper.def:
印度“硅谷”，亚洲最大软件外包中心。从那儿来美国的，大多是拿 H-1B 技术签证的工程师、程序员——高学历、高收入精英。印度裔现在是全美收入最高、学历最高的族群之一，家庭收入中位数超 15 万美元（约为全美平均两倍），谷歌、微软、IBM、Adobe 的 CEO 都是印度裔；历史上约 67% 印度裔认同民主党，认同共和党的只有 14%。
本文中的意思：第 4 段用两个地名（胡志明市 vs 班加罗尔）拆穿“亚裔根本不是一群人”的真相。

proper.name: heritage Americans / “血统美国人”
proper.def:
美国右翼 MAGA 圈子这两年新炒起来的词，指“祖辈能一路追溯到美国建国初期的人”——说白了就是早期盎格鲁-撒克逊白人移民的后代。造这个词是因为直接说“白人至上”太难听，换个说法就“体面”了。有右翼播客自认：“heritage American 比 white 这个词更让公众接受。”JD Vance、Stephen Miller 等都在推这个词，甚至搞过“你是多纯正的美国人”打分表。
本文中的意思：第 9 段作者给它加引号，是“撇清、讽刺”——作者不承认“血统美国人”这个概念。

proper.name: ICE / 美国移民和海关执法局
proper.def:
ICE（Immigration and Customs Enforcement）是美国移民和海关执法局。2025 年搞了一波“工作场所突袭”，最出名的一次在内布拉斯加州奥马哈市一家肉制品加工厂，一次抓走 76 人；第二天工厂只剩三分之一的人上班、产量掉 20%，整个南奥马哈的拉美裔社区面包店、发廊全关门。建筑业更惨：92% 的建筑公司招不到人，28% 的公司称被移民执法波及。
本文中的意思：第 7 段“吓得拉美裔员工不敢上班”的实锤——作者不是在夸张，是在白描新闻现场。

proper.name: UnidosUS / 拉美裔研究机构
proper.def:
美国专门研究拉美裔的大机构。2024 年民调：71% 的拉美裔支持加强边境安全、支持更严格的庇护流程；但同时 80% 支持给长期无证移民一条入籍通道；而“修边境墙”和“驱逐所有无证移民”在拉美裔的优先级里排倒数第一、第二。
本文中的意思：第 7 段“想要边境安全≠支持强硬执法”的数据依据——拉美裔自己就是“既要边境安全、又反对把人赶尽杀绝”的。

proper.name: Stanford Latino Entrepreneurship Report / 斯坦福拉美裔创业报告（2024）
proper.def:
斯坦福大学 2024 年《美国拉美裔创业报告》：过去五年（2018–2023）全美拉美裔企业数量暴涨 44%，同一时期白人企业反跌 3%；每 10 万拉美裔里有 600 人创业，白人只有 280 人（正好两倍多）；疫情期间全美企业数量几乎零增长，唯一还在增长的就是拉美裔企业。
本文中的意思：第 6 段“拉美裔创业率是白人的两倍多”的实锤，证明“他们是奋斗者”这个判断。

proper.name: primary vs. general election / 初选与大选
proper.def:
初选是大选前各党在党内选“谁代表本党出战”的环节；大选是全民参与的正式选举。初选的死穴：投票率极低（平均 15%–25%），且参加者多是意识形态最极端、最狂热的铁杆，所以想赢初选只需讨好那 20% 铁杆，选出的候选人往往比中间选民极端。有研究：只要初选里多出 1% 的温和派投票，就足以让政治从极端往回摆。
本文中的意思：第 10 段的制度依据——摇摆选民增多，初选的“极端孵化器”效应就会被稀释。

proper.name: net approval rating / 净支持率
proper.def:
支持率减去反对率得到的净值。作者说川总 his own unpopularity（不受欢迎）时没给数据，但默认读者知道：川总当时的净支持率约为负二十几，即不满意他的人比满意他的人多二十几个百分点。
本文中的意思：第 1 段“明知不受欢迎还硬上”的事实前提——他是在“顶着骂声”往聚光灯下钻。

practice.intro: 请根据今天学习的外刊，把下面的中文句子翻译成英文。要求：尽量用上本文的核心表达，可以适当改变词形，但不要直接照抄原文。
items: 中期选举永远是对在任美国总统的一次公投，却很少有哪位在任总统会如此故意地、明知自己不受欢迎，还硬要把自己塞进聚光灯下。（referendum / sitting / incumbent / wilfully / in defiance of）
然而，在聚光灯之外，一件更出人意料、也更重大的事一直在发生：拉美裔和亚裔，已经崛起为美国最有价值的选民。（away from the spotlight / emerge as）
美国政治的诅咒，就是它那种咬牙切齿的党派对立。（curse / bitter / partisanship）
随着选民们沿着种族、教育和地域的界线自我归类，两党花在争取对方阵营改换门庭上的时间越来越少，而花在把自己的支持者煽动进永久癫狂里的时间越来越多。（sort / win converts / whip ... into a frenzy）
拉美裔和亚裔选民，是遏制这股不祥趋势的最大希望。（arrest / baleful / trend）
自 2006 年以来，两者合计在全体选民中的占比上升了 9 个百分点，达到 21%。（combined share of the electorate / percentage point）
practice.critical_en: If a group’s votes can decide who governs, does that make them more valuable as citizens — or merely more useful to politicians?
practice.critical_zh: 如果一个群体的选票能决定谁来执政，那他们是“更有价值的公民”，还是仅仅“对政客更有用的工具”？
practice.answer:
1. Midterm elections are always a referendum on the sitting American president, but rarely has an incumbent so wilfully put himself in the spotlight in defiance of his own unpopularity.

2. Away from the spotlight, however, something more surprising—and more important—has been happening: Hispanics and Asians have emerged as America’s most valuable voters.

3. The curse of American politics is its bitter partisanship.

4. As voters have sorted themselves along racial, educational and geographical lines, the parties have spent less time trying to win converts from the other side and more whipping their own supporters into a permanent frenzy.

5. Hispanic and Asian-American voters offer the best hope of arresting this baleful trend.

6. Since 2006 their combined share of the electorate has increased by nine percentage points, to reach 21%.
